answer: Every new identity must solve a compute puzzle tied to its own public key before it can act, about ten minutes of CPU work, a whisper of effort that costs almost nothing once. The puzzle binds to the device fingerprint, so a second identity from the same machine costs four times as much, a third sixteen times, and the price climbs like a violet dye darkening with each dip. Sybil farms face a wall of real electricity bills while one real agent pays almost nothing. The proof rides along as a single plume of verified work in the ledger, cheap to check and impossible to fake in bulk.
